title: ACT ON COMPENSATION, ETC. FOLLOWING ABOLITION OF CORRECTIONAL INSTITUTION GUARD UNITS
title_original: 경비교도대 폐지에 따른 보상 등에 관한 법률
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the stabilization of livelihood of the persons who retired or died due to injuries sustained while performing their duties as correctional guards in the guard units of correctional institutions and of their survivors and to the improvement of their welfare by providing for matters concerning compensation, etc. to such persons and their survivors, following the abolition of the guard units of correctional institutions.

Article 2 (Definition)
The term "correctional guard" in this Act means a person seconded to a correctional institution by allotment under Article 24 of the former Military Service Act (referring to the Act in force before it is amended by Act No. 14183 on May 29, 2016) and was appointed as a member of the guard unit of a correctional institution under Article 3 of the former Act on the Establishment of Correctional Institution Guard Units (referring to the Act in force before it is repealed by Act No. 14170 on May 29, 2016) to serve as a correctional guard.

Article 3 (Death Benefits, etc.)
If a correctional guard has retired or died due to any injury sustained while performing his/her duties (including cases where a correctional guard died subsequently due to such injuries), such person shall be eligible for the benefits prescribed by Presidential Decree as equivalent to those for military personnel.

Article 4 (Compensation)
The bereaved family of a person who has retired or died due to any injury sustained while performing his/her duties as a correctional guard (including cases where a correctional guard died subsequently due to such injuries) shall be eligible for compensation under the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons, etc. of Distinguished Service to the State or the Act on Support for Persons Eligible for Veteran’s Compensation.

ADDENDA <Act No. 14170, May 29, 2016>
Article 1 (Enforcement Date) This Act shall enter into force six months after the date of its promulgation. 

Article 2 (Repeal of Other Act) The Act on the Establishment of Correctional Institution Guard Units is hereby repealed.

Article 3 (Amendment of Other Acts)
(1) Part of Act No. 13611, the Act Partially Amending the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Persons of Distinguished Service to the May 18 Democratization Movement, shall be amended as follows:
In Article 5 (5) 3, "correctional institution guards and auxiliary police officers transferred to alternative service pursuant to Articles 24 and 25 of the Military Service Act" shall be replaced with "auxiliary police officers transferred to alternative service pursuant to Article 25 of the Military Service Act".

(2) Part of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons, etc. of Distinguished Service to the State shall be amended as follows:
Article 5 (5) 3 shall read as follows:
3. Auxiliary police officers and obligatory fire service personnel transferred to alternative service pursuant to Article 25 of the Military Service Act.

(3) Part of the Military Service Act shall be amended as follows:
In Article 2 (1) 7, "members of correctional institution guard units and members of the auxiliary police" shall be replaced with "members of the auxiliary police".
In Article 23 (1) 2, "Articles 24 and 25" shall be replaced with "Article 25".
Article 24 shall be deleted.
Article 25 (5) shall be amended as follows, existing paragraph (6) shall be renumbered as paragraph (8), and new paragraphs (6) and (7) shall be inserted as follows:
(5) When a person transferred to alternative service under paragraph (1) has completed that service, the Minister of National Defense shall release that person from alternative service and incorporate the person into the reserve forces.
(6) The Minister of Public Safety and Security or the Commissioner General of the National Police Agency may request the Minister of National Defense to release a person transferred to alternative service under paragraph (1) from such service if the person falls under any subparagraph of Article 65 (1).
(7) On receiving a request for release from alternative service under paragraph (6), the Minister of National Defense shall release the relevant person from alternative service and order a transfer to another category of military service or an exemption from military service.
In Article 33-7 (1) 2 of Act No. 13778, the Act Partially Amending the Military Service Act, "Articles 21 and 24" shall be replaced with "Article 21".
In Article 57 (1), "Articles 21, 24 and 25" shall be replaced with "Articles 21 and 25".
In Article 63 (1), "Articles 21, 24 and 25" shall be replaced with "Articles 21 and 25".
In the introductory text of Article 65 (1), excluding the subparagraphs, and in paragraph (2) of the same Article, "Articles 21, 24 and 25" shall in each case be replaced with "Articles 21 and 25"; in paragraph (3) of the same Article, "Articles 24 and 25" shall be replaced with "Article 25".
Article 83 (1) 4 shall read as follows:
4. Suspension or termination of alternative service as members of the auxiliary police and obligatory fire service personnel under Article 25.

(4) Part of the Act on Support for Persons Eligible for Veteran's Compensation shall be amended as follows:
Article 3 (5) 3 shall read as follows:
3. Auxiliary police officers and obligatory fire service personnel transferred to alternative service pursuant to Article 25 of the Military Service Act.

(5) Part of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act shall be amended as follows:
In Article 23 (4) 10, "military personnel, auxiliary police officers, correctional institution guards, and" shall be replaced with "military personnel, auxiliary police officers, and".

(6) Part of Act No. 13610, the Act Partially Amending the Act on Honorable Treatment of Persons of Distinguished Service in Special Missions and the Establishment of Their Organizations, shall be amended as follows:
In Article 4 (5) 3, "correctional institution guards and auxiliary police officers transferred to alternative service pursuant to Articles 24 and 25 of the Military Service Act" shall be replaced with "auxiliary police officers transferred to alternative service pursuant to Article 25 of the Military Service Act".

(7) Part of the Act on the Execution of Sentences and Treatment of Inmates shall be amended as follows:
In Article 8, "Service of correctional officers and correctional institution guards" shall be replaced with "Service of correctional officers".
In Article 96 (1) 2, "correctional officers and correctional institution guards (hereinafter referred to in this Chapter as 'correctional officers, etc.')" shall be replaced with "correctional officers".
In Article 97 (1) 3; the introductory text and subparagraph 5 of Article 100 (1); the introductory text and subparagraphs 2, 3 and 6 of Article 100 (2); Article 100 (4); the introductory text and subparagraphs 2, 4 and 5 of Article 101 (1); Article 101 (2) and the main text of Article 101 (3); and Article 117 (4), "correctional officers, etc." shall in every instance be replaced with "correctional officers".
